questions.q: Describe the efforts of nineteenth-century reformers to improve the condition of women.
answer: Nineteenth-century reformers worked hard to end social evils that oppressed women.

answer.text: Raja Rammohan Roy, founder of the Brahmo Samaj in 1828, campaigned against the practice of sati, using ancient texts and reason to show it was wrong. Largely through his efforts, sati was banned in 1829.
Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar argued that the remarriage of widows was sanctioned by the shastras, and his campaign led to the Widow Remarriage Act of 1856.
Reformers also promoted the education of girls, opening schools for them, and opposed child marriage, an effort that later led to laws raising the age of marriage.

answer: These efforts slowly changed attitudes towards women.

questions.q: How did reformers challenge caste inequality in the nineteenth century?
answer: Alongside efforts for women, reformers attacked the injustices of the caste system.

answer.text: Jyotirao Phule attacked the domination of the upper castes, founded the Satyashodhak Samaj in 1873, and wrote Gulamgiri. With Savitribai Phule he opened schools for girls and for lower-caste children.

In the south, E.V. Ramaswamy Naicker, known as Periyar, led the Self-Respect Movement against caste and Brahmin dominance, while Dr B.R. Ambedkar organised the Depressed Classes to fight for temple entry, access to wells and human dignity.
Organisations such as the Arya Samaj and the Ramakrishna Mission also worked against caste discrimination, helping to spread the idea of equality.

questions.q: How did the spread of print and new ideas help the movement for social reform in the nineteenth century?

answer.text: The growth of newspapers, journals, books and pamphlets in Indian languages let reformers reach a wide public, debate customs openly, and mobilise opinion against practices they saw as unjust.

list: Reformers like Raja Rammohun Roy used writings to argue against sati, citing ancient texts to show it had no religious sanction, helping bring its ban in 1829
Ishwarchandra Vidyasagar campaigned through pamphlets for widow remarriage, backed by law in 1856
Debates in the press spread ideas about women's education and against child marriage

answer.lead: Print thus turned private customs into public issues,
answer.text: letting reformers appeal to both scriptures and reason to change society and pressure the government to legislate.

questions.q: How did leaders from within oppressed castes work to demand equality and dignity?

answer.lead: Change came from below as well.
answer.text: Members of oppressed castes organised themselves to challenge caste injustice and claim rights, not just relying on upper-caste reformers.

list: Jyotirao Phule attacked claims of Brahmanical superiority and, with Savitribai Phule, opened schools for girls and lower-caste children
In western India, non-Brahman movements demanded a fair share in jobs and respect
In the south, Periyar (E.V. Ramasamy Naicker) led the Self-Respect Movement against caste and untouchability
B.R. Ambedkar organised movements for temple entry and against untouchability, insisting on equal rights

answer.text: linked social reform to the demands of the marginalised themselves, making caste equality central to the idea of a just India.
